ordinary_strict_equivalence.classification: New merged book theorem asserted by upstream, not a theorem replayed or independently proved by this monitor.
ordinary_strict_equivalence.stated_scope: Characteristic-zero coefficient field k; n>=1, nonzero homogeneous F of degree d>0, q>=1, homogeneous A of degree d(q+1)-(n+1). Smoothness and irreducibility are not required for the algebraic strictification statement. It is existence equivalence with unrestricted legal denominator, staying over k.
ordinary_strict_equivalence.conclusion: From an ordinary homogeneous certificate, the book constructs a normalized strict field satisfying q*v(F)=A and div(v)=0.
ordinary_strict_equivalence.denominator: Starting from homogeneous denominator D of degree e, choose a coordinate u with nonzero constant u^d leading coefficient of F. Set Delta=Res_u(F,D). The claimed legal homogeneous denominator Delta^q has degree d*q*e. Support may change; this is not preservation of D or of its original ambient open.
ordinary_strict_equivalence.parity: Optional involution averaging preserves strictness for even F/odd A, but multiplying by the conjugate denominator can further increase degree and lose the intermediate u-degree bound.
ordinary_strict_equivalence.fixed_denominator_limit: Full quotient Q remains necessary for a general fixed-D search. The special conical case preserves the supplied denominator only when D is independent of the chosen u and F has constant nonzero u^d coefficient; preserving D^2 does not establish existence over D.
ordinary_strict_equivalence.normal_form_limit: Reducing all current components modulo f^q gives u-degree<q*deg(f), with the source bound degree_u(P)<(q+1)*deg(f). Denominators in the remaining coefficient field stay unrestricted. This reduction does not assert existence.
ordinary_strict_equivalence.gauge_correction: Chapter1 now explicitly says D -> D+tF preserves coprimality as well as the divisor on X, although it need not preserve strictness of the individual witness. Chapter5 says resultant support is invariant under same-degree D -> D+FG (up to scalar; exact for monic F).
ordinary_strict_equivalence.fixed_open_limit: The added de Rham comparison distinguishes a regular error form from an exact one. Strictification removes the particular ambient obstruction after controlled support change; it does not make arbitrary regular top forms rationally exact.

summary: Chapter3 adds normal-bundle trace pairings and a curve-family criterion detecting a nonzero supported Hodge image. At a fixed fourfold, nonzero pullback does not alone show the particular input belongs to that image; actual algebraic curve motions are required.

Chapter4 makes the polarizable-subvariation formulation explicit and adds a conditional dominant smooth-incidence criterion, parity/interpolation restrictions, and rank conditions. It does not assert existence of a dominating construction, and tangent rank on an unverified/nonreduced scheme is insufficient.

Chapter5 adds finite rational-exactness tests for a supplied curve/differential, with all poles including infinity retained. Zero residues alone do not suffice, and this gives no bound for an unknown higher-dimensional support.

The cubic-current scalar reduction remains an equivalence of rational differential equations over unrestricted base-coordinate functions, not a claim that the remaining scalar equation is always solvable.
